wu: Start with 'Yesterday's Timeline': Students draw 3 simple activities they did yesterday on a paper timeline. They share with a partner using 'I was...ing' (e.g., 'I was eating lunch at 1 PM').
wuAlt: 'Find Someone Who Was...' mingle: Students ask 'Were you...ing yesterday?' (e.g., 'Were you watching TV?') and find classmates who say yes.
'Picture Prompt': Show a busy street photo; students guess what people were doing using 'He/She was...ing'.
pres: Present a short comic strip of a Moroccan souk scene with speech bubbles. Model sentences like 'While I was buying spices, the merchant was weighing dates.' Use flashcards of actions (buying, walking, talking) and elicit 'was/were + -ing'. Check comprehension with thumbs up/down for true/false sentences about the story.
presAlt: Use a realia box with Moroccan items (tea set, mint, babouches) to act out a story: 'While I was pouring tea, my friend was eating cookies.'
Show a 1-minute video clip of a busy market in Oujda; pause to ask 'What was he/she doing?'
prac: Play 'Past Continuous Chain': Students sit in a circle. Student 1 starts with 'I was walking to school.' Student 2 says 'While he was walking to school, I was buying bread.' Continue the chain. Monitor for correct 'when/while' usage.
pracAlt: 'Sentence Race': Write two columns on the board (was/were). In teams, students race to write correct past continuous sentences about a picture (e.g., 'The boy was riding a bike').
'Matching Pairs': Match past continuous sentence halves (e.g., 'While the teacher was talking' + 'the students were taking notes').
ls: Listen to a short audio diary of a teen's day at the American Space Oujda. Students fill in blanks with past continuous verbs (e.g., 'While I was ___ the computer, my friend was ___ a book'). Play twice; check answers in pairs.
re: Play 'Freeze Frame': Call out an action (e.g., 'You were eating!'). Students freeze in a pose and say what they were doing. After the break, restart with a new action.
prod: Roleplay 'Cafe Chaos': In pairs, one is a waiter, one is a customer. The waiter asks 'What were you doing when the order came wrong?' The customer responds with past continuous. Swap roles. Encourage follow-up questions like 'Why were you laughing?'
rw: Read a short fable 'The Hare and the Tortoise' with past simple and continuous highlighted. Students underline all 'was/were + -ing' and write 3 sentences explaining what the hare was doing (e.g., 'While the tortoise was walking slowly, the hare was sleeping').
st: Tell a simple story about a Moroccan wedding using past continuous: 'While the family was dancing, the bride was smiling.' End with a quick recap: 'Today we told stories about what was happening.'
g: Students sit in a circle and pass a ball, saying a past continuous sentence about the person next to them (e.g., 'You were smiling').
Show a busy photo; teams race to write 5 past continuous sentences about it.
Teacher mimes an action; students guess 'Were you...ing?' and the teacher responds.
Students act out an action; others guess using 'He/She was...ing'.
Roll a dice; land on a square and make a sentence with 'when' or 'while' using past continuous.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 4-sentence story about a Moroccan festival (e.g., Green March) using past continuous.
Support learners: Use a sentence frame: 'While I was ___, my friend was ___' with word bank.
hw: Complete the 'Past Continuous Stories' worksheet from the library folder (fill in gaps with was/were + -ing).
Write 8 sentences about what you and your family were doing during last Friday's prayer time.
Draw a comic strip of 3 panels showing what was happening during a power cut at home; label with past continuous.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural contexts (souks, weddings, festivals) to make past continuous relatable. Teens engage more with stories they recognize.
